preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(x) <= 3 * 10**5 for x in stdin.split() if x.isdigit())
preconditions.description: All integers in input are within bounds 1 ≤ n, q, a_i, x_i, y_i, u_i, v_i, l_i, r_i ≤ 3⋅10^5.
Input format is correct: first line n and q, second line n integers a_i, followed by (n-1) lines of edges, then q lines of queries.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= a_i <= n for a_i in map(int, stdin.split()[2:2+n]))
preconditions.description: Each city's mineral resource label a_i is between 1 and n.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x_i < y_i <= n for x_i, y_i in zip(map(int, stdin.split()[2+n+2*i:2+n+2*i+2]) for i in range(n-1)))
preconditions.description: Edges form a tree with unique undirected connections between distinct cities.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u_i <= n and 1 <= v_i <= n and 1 <= l_i <= r_i <= n for u_i, v_i, l_i, r_i in zip(map(int, stdin.split()[2+n+2*(n-1)+4*i:2+n+2*(n-1)+4*i+4]) for i in range(q)))
preconditions.description: Each query has valid city indices u_i, v_i and bounds l_i ≤ r_i.

postconditions.description: Each output line contains exactly one integer (either -1 or a valid mineral resource).

postconditions.expression: all(stdout_line.strip() in ['-1'] or (1 <= int(stdout_line.strip()) <= n) for stdout_line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each output is either -1 or a mineral resource label between 1 and n.

postconditions.expression: all((c_i == -1) or (l_i <= c_i <= r_i) for (u_i, v_i, l_i, r_i), c_i in zip([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2+n+2*(n-1)+i:2+n+2*(n-1)+i+1]] for i in range(q)), map(int, stdout.splitlines())))
postconditions.description: If c_i is not -1, it lies within the query's bounds l_i ≤ c_i ≤ r_i.

postconditions.expression: all((c_i == -1) or (count_odd_on_path(u_i, v_i, c_i, a, tree) for (u_i, v_i, l_i, r_i), c_i in zip([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2+n+2*(n-1)+i:2+n+2*(n-1)+i+1]] for i in range(q)), map(int, stdout.splitlines())))
postconditions.description: If c_i is not -1, it appears an odd number of times on the path between u_i and v_i in the tree. (count_odd_on_path(u, v, c, a, tree) is true iff the count of c in the path from u to v is odd.)

postconditions.expression: all((c_i == -1) or (any(c == c_i and l_i <= c <= r_i and count_odd_on_path(u_i, v_i, c, a, tree) for c in set(a))) for (u_i, v_i, l_i, r_i), c_i in zip([tuple(map(int, line.split())) for line in stdin.splitlines()[2+n+2*(n-1)+i:2+n+2*(n-1)+i+1]] for i in range(q)), map(int, stdout.splitlines())))
postconditions.description: If c_i is not -1, it is a valid mineral resource satisfying the query's conditions (exists in a, within bounds, and odd count on path).
